skills.skill: I can find the five-figure summary and interquartile range.

items.src: Cambridge Essential Mathematics 9 (3rd Ed), Ch 9 review, multiple-choice Q9 (p. 714)

items.q:
Find the five-number summary for this ordered data set.
$7, 9, 11, 12, 13, 13, 18, 19, 35, 42, 45, 46, 61, 62, 78$
sol: $Q_1 = 12$ (middle of the lower $7$), $Q_3 = 46$ (middle of the upper $7$)
items.src: Oxford Maths 10 VC (2022), Exercise 10A Q2b (p. 504); adapted: stem reworded for a single part

items.q: A data set has $14$ values. Which of the following is correct?
options: The median and both upper and lower quartiles are values in the set.
The median is a value in the set, but the upper and lower quartiles are not.
The upper and lower quartiles are values in the set, but the median is not.
None of the median, upper or lower quartiles are values in the set.
The median and the upper quartile are values in the set, but the lower quartile is not.
sol: Median = average of the $7$th and $8$th values (not a value in the set)
Each half has $7$ values, so $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ are the $4$th value of each half (C)
items.src: Oxford Maths 10 VC (2022), Ch 10 review, multiple-choice Q1 (p. 565)
Cambridge Essential Mathematics 8 (3rd Ed), Exercise 8E Q2a (p. 578); adapted: stem reworded for a single part

items.q:
Find the IQR of the following set. Remember to sort first.
$6, 11, 3, 15, 18, 14, 13, 2, 16, 7, 7$
items.src: Cambridge Essential Mathematics 8 (3rd Ed), Exercise 8E Q5c (p. 578); adapted: stem reworded for a single part

skills.skill: I can find any outliers in a data set.

items.q:
The data below represents the data collected over a month of $30$ consecutive days of the delay time (in minutes) of the flight departures of the same evening flight for airline A.
2116141817412149213419
1317352241912140713181238
Does the data for airline A appear to have any outliers (numbers not near the majority of data elements)?
sol: Yes: $52$ is an outlier (the other values are all between $0$ and $24$).
items.src: Cambridge Essential Mathematics 9 (3rd Ed), Ch 9 review, extended-response Q2a (p. 715); adapted: stem reworded for a single part

items.q:
Consider this data set: $2, 6, 3, 8, 9, 10, 14, 19, 4, 8, 22, 11, 13, 17, 4, 19, 7, 7, 10$.
Find the lower quartile, median and upper quartile, calculate the values of the lower and upper fences, and determine whether there are any outliers in this data set.
items.src: Oxford Maths 10 VC (2022), Exercise 10B Q2b–d (p. 509); adapted: parts b–d combined

items.q:
Consider the frequency table showing the number of aces served by a tennis player.
AcesFrequency
01
13
24
32
46
51
101
a  Construct a dot plot for the frequency table.
b  Use your dot plot to identify any outliers.
sol: b $10$ aces is an outlier: it is separated from the main cluster ($0$ to $5$).
items.src: Cambridge Essential Mathematics 8 (3rd Ed), Exercise 8C Q2a, c (p. 564); adapted: parts chosen
